A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same stereo-matching work and contain readable text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary material. Existing content can be reliably matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original generalization experiments, component ablations, memory measurements, and qualitative analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds Flickr1024 predictions and quantitative results from additional TranScene training.

M1.justification: The monocular encoder, local ordering maps, Beta guidance, iterative updates, registration, confidence fusion, and losses remain unchanged. The explicit Gamma-based sampling formula clarifies the existing Beta sampler. TranScene introduces an additional training setting rather than a new model component or objective.

E1.justification: v2 substantially extends training and evaluation coverage: Section 9 adds synthetic transparent-scene training through TranScene, and Section 6 adds qualitative evaluation on diverse Flickr1024 photographs. All previous datasets remain. Despite TranScene's multiple depth labels, the added experiment selects one disparity target and retains the single-disparity task.

E2.justification: The benchmark, memory, and backbone comparisons retain their comparator sets. MASt3R was already evaluated in v1 despite its missing citations. Ours+TranScene is an additional training condition for the proposed model, not a newly evaluated competing algorithm.

E3.justification: The added TranScene experiment uses SceneFlow-pretrained weights, end-to-end training instead of the original staged strategy, and the largest-disparity label in transparent regions. Tables 10–11 also introduce Booster RMSE and 6-/8-pixel error rates. Previously reported experimental protocols are retained.

E4.justification: Section 9 and Tables 10–11 add an analysis of additional-data training, separating transparent/nontransparent regions and material classes. This tests an additional scalability question, although training strategy also changes. Existing component ablations, memory analyses, intermediate visualizations, and failure cases are preserved.

E5.justification: Both versions report ablation means and standard deviations across the 80k, 90k, and 100k training checkpoints. v2 introduces no new seed counts, independent-run information, confidence intervals, or significance tests; its added benchmark results use point estimates.

E6.justification: All eleven original tables retain their numerical values after matching renumbered tables. v2 adds substantial results for the TranScene-trained variant: Table 10 reports overall Booster EPE of 1.24 versus 2.26 and transparent-region EPE of 5.67 versus 7.93. These compare different training conditions, not revised same-setting scores. Flickr1024 predictions and additional metric entries are also new.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6 retain the same mathematical definitions and objectives, with no added theorem, proof, or substantive derivation. The Gamma-ratio expression explains implementation of the already specified Beta sampler rather than introducing new mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: ordering-based local fusion, registration-based global fusion, improved generalization, and limited computational overhead. Their claims about results without additional stereo data still refer to the retained SceneFlow-only experiments.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of Flickr1024 robustness and scalability with additional transparent-scene data. Section 9 claims improvement across all evaluated metrics, but Table 11 contains exceptions, including class-1 RMSE increasing from 4.70 to 4.74. Existing explanations and limitations concerning transparency and dark scenes remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 specifies the Gamma construction used to sample Beta guidance and documents TranScene label selection and initialization. It adds demo and model-weight download links alongside the retained repository link, and states that project code covers the ablations. These are documented access pointers; external availability was not checked.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for TranScene and Flickr1024 and supplies MASt3R/DUSt3R references where v1 had unresolved citations. The relationship to existing stereo and monocular-fusion research remains substantively unchanged despite condensed related-work prose.

P1.justification: v2 condenses related work and some introductory prose, clarifies method terminology and sampling, and adds author contact information and acknowledgements. The supplement gains introductory material and numbered sections replacing lettered appendices, while the existing narrative order is largely preserved.

P2.justification: v2 adds the Flickr1024 montage in Figure 5, two TranScene comparison tables, and resource badges and a supplementary title block. Some existing displays are resized or relocated, including Table 4 moving to page 7. Existing figure imagery and table contents are otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful qualitative coverage and evidence about additional transparent-scene training, while clearer sampling details, repaired citations, and resource links improve documentation. The gain is limited: the TranScene experiment changes both data and training strategy, preventing a clean data-only interpretation, and its claim of improvement across all metrics overlooks regressions in Table 11. The central method and original validation remain unchanged.
